hints: After each new score you only need the score in k-th place. Do you really need to remember the scores that are already below k-th place?
Keep only the k largest scores seen so far in a min-heap. The smallest of those k (the heap top) is exactly the k-th largest overall.

1. Constructor: store k and an empty min-heap; call add logic for each score in nums.
  2. add(val): push val.
  3. If the heap now has more than k items, pop the smallest.
  4. Return the heap top.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Keep every score in a list; on each add, sort the list in descending order and read index k−1.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: A min-heap capped at size k holds the top k scores; its top is the k-th largest.

explain: With k = 2 and scores [10,4,7], the heap keeps {7,10} (4 is dropped). add(5): 5 goes in and is popped right away, answer 7. add(12): heap becomes {10,12}, answer 10. add(11): {11,12}, answer 11. add(1): 1 is popped immediately, answer stays 11. Invariant: the heap always holds the k largest scores so far. Edge case: nums may start with fewer than k scores, so pop only when the size goes above k.
recognize: A stream of values and 'k-th largest so far' asked again and again → a min-heap of size k.
